name: is-the-favourite-row-even-offered
description:
Separates two failures that look identical from outside: the favourite ROW never arrived in the palette, or it arrived and Return did not accept it. A sibling scenario reports only that no accept reached the browser, which is true either way, and its sibling absence assertion passes in both - so the scenario reads '5 passed, 1 failed' whichever is wrong.

Reads the palette's own DOM before pressing Return. The command bar is its own surface, so the eval targets /commandbar rather than the sidebar.

The original sanity pairing compared the total row count against the favourite count and required them to differ, to catch a run where every eval returned one stored value. It was the wrong instrument: with the fix in place the palette offers exactly one row and it IS the favourite, so 1 and 1 are correct and the assertion failed on a healthy run. Naming the top row's text makes the same independence point and asserts something real.

actions.note: let the sidebar render and the startup tab commit, so the favourite has a live tab to activate
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
let the palette's WebContents commit and take the field
the autocomplete pass and the favourite rows land together
the favourite row, labelled, at the top
how many rows the palette is offering at the moment Return is about to be pressed
and how many of them are FAVOURITES - the row the accept is supposed to take
what the top row actually says, since Return accepts the top one
accept the top row, which is the favourite

assertions.note: THE QUESTION. One favourite row must be offered before Return is pressed. If this is 0 the accept had nothing to take and the defect is upstream of the keypress.

Return accepts the TOP row, so naming it is the claim that matters. It also keeps the reads honest in a way a count cannot: this returns a string from a different query than the counts above, so a run where every eval handed back one stored value fails here.
